title: Acute PE — 2026 AHA/ACC Guideline
sources: Critical Vector — 2026 AHA/ACC Acute PE Guideline journal-club cheat sheet

Creager MA, Barnes GD, Giri J, et al. 2026 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ACEP/CHEST/SCAI/SHM/SIR/SVM/SVN Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults. Circulation 2026;153:e977–e1051. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001415

changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from the CV cheat sheet of the 2026 multi-society Acute PE guideline. New A–E clinical categories replace massive/submassive; half-dose DOAC extended phase; RV/LV ratio reporting Class 1; normotensive shock (D2).

summary: The 2026 multi-society guideline scrapped 'massive / submassive / low risk' (and the ESC four-tier scheme) for AHA/ACC Acute PE Clinical Categories A–E, each with subcategories, plus an optional 'R' modifier for respiratory failure. Diagnosis is largely unchanged; the new ideas are the taxonomy, 'normotensive shock' (D2), and half-dose DOAC for the extended phase.

body.text: Journal-club summary of a 75-page guideline, not a substitute for the source text — verify class/level ratings before clinical application. The A–E taxonomy has not been prospectively validated (the writing committee's own top evidence gap), and many advanced-therapy recommendations remain C-LD or B-NR.
The new severity taxonomy — Categories A–E

rows: Incidental, asymptomatic — found on a CT ordered for something else (e.g. cancer staging).
Symptomatic but PESI ≤ 85 / sPESI 0 / Hestia negative. B1 = subsegmental clot, B2 = more proximal.
C1 normal RV + biomarkers · C2 one abnormal · C3 both abnormal.
D1 transient hypotension · D2 = 'normotensive shock' — hypoperfusing quietly with a normal BP.
E1 shock with a pulse, on pressors · E2 refractory shock or arrest.

body.text: Add 'R' for hypoxemia, tachypnea, or an oxygen requirement (e.g. C3R, D2R). The taxonomy maps onto the treatment algorithm in the guideline's Figure 3 — the single most useful chart in the document.

items: Wells / Geneva / PERC + age-adjusted D-dimer + YEARS still drive imaging decisions — no change.
CTPA still beats V/Q for confirming the diagnosis.
Upgrade: reporting a NUMERICAL RV/LV ratio off CTPA is now Class 1 — the subjective eyeball assessment is out.
Echo still cannot diagnose PE — strictly for risk stratification once PE is confirmed.
PESI / sPESI / Hestia are good at finding who is SAFE to send home (Class 1 for Category A/B). No score reliably predicts who is about to crash — stated plainly in the guideline.
Troponin + BNP + lactate: Class 1 for anyone Category C or higher.
RV imaging: Class 1 for Categories C–D.

rows: Outpatient territory — send home, start a DOAC.
Admit and work up — LMWH initiation, biomarkers + RV imaging. PERT consult is reasonable.
Advanced therapy enters the conversation. Vasopressors (norepinephrine first-line) for D2. Look for the 'normotensive shock' pattern before it declares itself.
Full advanced-therapy conversation. PERT is Class 1. VA-ECMO for E2. Systemic lysis / catheter-directed lysis / mechanical thrombectomy / surgical embolectomy all reasonable at E1.

body.text: The C2–D2 zone is exactly the population enrolled in PEERLESS, which found no mortality or bleeding difference between catheter-directed lysis and mechanical thrombectomy (more bailout to alternate therapy in the CDL arm). Surgery without mechanical support at E2 is now Class 3 — no benefit.

items: LMWH over UFH for initial parenteral therapy (Class 1).
DOAC over VKA for most patients (Class 1) — EXCEPT antiphospholipid syndrome, where VKA is preferred (arterial thrombosis risk with DOACs).
Brain tumors: DOAC now PREFERRED over LMWH to reduce ICH risk — a flip from older teaching.
Pregnancy: LMWH / UFH only. DOACs and warfarin are Class 3 — harm.

Extended-phase anticoagulation for unprovoked PE: continue indefinitely. NEW — half-dose DOAC (apixaban 2.5 mg BID or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily) is Class 1 for the extended phase, cutting bleeding without losing efficacy (RENOVE, API-CAT).
IVC filters: retrievable over permanent, pull as soon as safe. Placing one in a patient already therapeutically anticoagulated is Class 3 — harm.

body.text: Anything that blunts sympathetic tone — induction agents, positive-pressure ventilation — can trigger arrest in a compensated PE patient. Deep sedation and mechanical ventilation are Class 3 — harm — unless clinically necessary; if unavoidable, have pressors, inotropes, and/or ECMO ready at the bedside first.

items: Ask about dyspnea at every visit for a year.
Workup requires TTE + a perfusion scan + CPET — no single test rules it out.
Routine repeat CTPA to check clot resolution is explicitly called out as NOT useful.
